questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: It rarely happens to trucks.
It usually happens when vehicles travel faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water instead of the road. You do not need a lot of water for this to occur. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, it saves time.
No, it is dangerous.
Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, and drinking are distracting activities that should not be done while driving. Plan ahead and stop to eat on long trips.

questions.question: How should you do a standard parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it while keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?

options.text: The driver
The mechanic
The owner

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe operation. Check your vehicle before driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks?

options.text: The vehicle will have no brakes.
The vehicle will still have brakes.
The vehicle will go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: The ABS system helps prevent wheel lockup. If it fails, the basic brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What should you know about people working on disabled vehicles?

options.text: They are probably watching the road.
They may be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
They do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on disabled vehicles. They are focused on repairs and may not pay attention to traffic nearby.

questions.question: How can you avoid driving aggressively?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Judge other drivers' abilities.
Plan realistic travel times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan realistic travel times.
questions.explanation: To avoid frustration that leads to aggressive driving, plan ahead with realistic travel times. Allow extra time for traffic delays. Also drive at safe speeds, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and avoid making gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: What should happen when you start a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The brakes should lock up.
The ABS light should turn on, then turn off quickly.
The steering wheel will not move until air tanks are full.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS light should turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, the ABS indicator light should come on and then turn off. If it stays on, the ABS is not working correctly.

questions.question: What should you do if suspension parts are broken?

options.text: Fix them right away.
Fix them, but there is no rush.
You cannot identify broken suspension parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix them right away.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: What tread depth is needed in front tire grooves?

options.text: 1/32 of an inch
2/32 of an inch
4/32 of an inch

questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires must have 4/32 of an inch tread depth in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, how should you start?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharp as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse your steering to follow it.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Open the hood right away.
Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine immediately to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless you need to.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To stay in control of the vehicle.
To not go faster than the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stay in control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery roads. Too much power can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: What happens if an engine has no oil?

options.text: The vehicle will use less gas.
The engine can be destroyed quickly.
The ABS will not work right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: Your engine needs oil pressure to work. Running an engine without oil will destroy it fast.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?

options.text: One-half or more.
About one-third.
About one-quarter.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-half or more.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when road surfaces have poor traction. On packed snow, cut your speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: When driving on a surface with poor traction, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To stay in control of the vehicle.
To not go faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stay in control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on roads with poor traction, like rain or snow, to avoid losing control.

questions.question: If vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a multilane road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Drive on the shoulder.
Use the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the right lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is slow. This lets other vehicles pass you in the left lane.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How much you drink
How often you drink
The temperature of the drink

questions.correctAnswerText: How much you drink
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends mainly on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: Which is not a good way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Watch the gauges.
Use your senses.
Check important items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle during the trip, not just at the start and end. Watch the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: Regrooved tires should not be used where?

options.text: On any vehicle.
On the front wheels of a bus.
On trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.
